newsitem.title: USA: USDA pegs Brazil 96/97 coffee crop at 27 mln bags.
newsitem.headline: USDA pegs Brazil 96/97 coffee crop at 27 mln bags.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Friday reiterated that its forecast for Brazil 1996/97 coffee output was 27 million 60-kilogram bags.

"The official USDA estimate for coffee production in Brazil in the 1996/97 marketing year is 27.0 million bags, that is the estimate that was released by the USDA on December 13, that is still the current estimate and we have no plans to revise that estimate before our next estimate is released next June," USDA analyst Edmond Missiaen told Reuters.
Missiaen is the specialty crops analysts at USDA's World Agricultural Outlook Board.

Earlier, coffee futures on New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange rallied more than three cents per lb on a report by a U.S. agricultural attache posted to the U.S. embassy in Sao Paulo that forecast the Brazil coffee crop would be lower.
The report, dated November 5, was made available in Washington on Friday.

Missiaen noted USDA does not allow release of coffee and cocoa attaches ahead of department reports on those commodities. On Dec. 13 USDA released its semi-annual world coffee production forecast and later Friday its Tropical Products report will provide additional information on coffee.
Missiaen said USDA uses attache reports from the field and the analysis of experts in Washington to come up with its forecasts.

"In fact, if you talked to the attache now, he's using the 27 (million bag Brazil estimate). We talk to the attache before we make a major change from what he or she reports. He hasn't written that down any place but if you asked him what he's using that's what he'll say is the estimate," Missiaen added.
The market retreated from its highs once the USDA reiterated its forecast.
